news.title: LWN.net Weekly Edition for November 5, 2026
news.abstract: Welcome to the LWN.net Weekly Edition for November 5, 2026 This edition contains the following feature content: Containers as a recognized kernel object : Josef Bacik has proposed a container abstraction called "cells", which would turn containers into first-class kernel objects. LLM reviews for Debian's new queue spark debate : after feedback, maintainers can now opt-out of LLM-generated emails, but questions remain. System-call wrappers for glibc : making kernel functionality easier to use from the C library. Removing binder.c : the journey to replace the kernel's Binder driver with a Rust implementation. Managing the kernel CVE flood : one vendor's approach to coping with the storm of kernel CVEs. Plasma X11 session removal surprises some Fedora users : a mid-release update obsoleted Plasma X11 packages for Fedora Linux 44 users. The second part of the 7.4 merge window : the rest of the changes headed into the next kernel release. Portable Python scripts with dependencies : a look at the standard for declaring a Python script's dependencies, and some of the implementations. This week's edition also includes these inner pages: Brief items : Brief news items from throughout the co
news.summary: 本期为LWN周报索引，核心是“cells”容器对象提案：在现有命名空间、cgroup和沙箱机制之上，尝试建立内核识别的一等容器抽象；另涉及glibc系统调用封装、Binder驱动Rust化及7.4合并窗口。内容未明确涉及网络子系统、eBPF/XDP、网卡驱动、RDMA/DPDK或容器网络数据面，也没有网络方法的性能评估结论。
